why: B is false (not_B, #rt_check OK) at n = 0: M = ℝ⁰ (the open slice submanifold univ ⊆ ℝ⁰ via RoundTrip.Bridge) is compact and connected, the positivity hypothesis K(U,U) > 0 for U ≠ 0 is vacuous, but B also demands that the minimum (n−1)/r² be attained at a unit vector U₀ (‖U₀‖ = 1 in the Riemannian norm), and T_pM = 0 has none. So ¬(A → B), and B → A holds ex falso. For n = 1 B is vacuous (K ≡ 0); Milnor means n ≥ 2. A (universes 0) holds for slice submanifolds N ⊆ V with dim ≥ 2: continuity of (q,u) ↦ tr(W ↦ R(u,W)u), the existence of r > 0 with K ≥ (n−1)/r² (compact N, positive Ricci; not that it is attained), and the index estimate index ≥ k for length > kπr under K ≥ (n−1)/r² for ANY N (no compactness), with two corollaries. On the repaired, embedded B (n ≥ 2) A implies B (A_to_B_emb2 below); the converse would need the reverse Hessian dictionary and only covers compact N.
B_issue: False for n = 0: the clause 'with equality for some unit U₀' (Milnor's 'takes on a minimum') needs a unit tangent vector, which a 0-dimensional M lacks, while the positivity hypothesis is vacuous there. Fix: assume 2 ≤ n (Milnor's (n−1)/r² > 0 presupposes it; for n = 1 B is vacuous anyway).
